experimental_design.evidence: inferred: In-cell LiP-MS captured the known binding of rapamycin to FKBP1A within the cell and detected global protein structural alterations upon sodium arsenite treatment.
inferred: We detected known and novel structural alterations of proteins from stress granules as well as from nuclear speckles and validated alteration of nuclear speckles by fluorescence microscopy.

factor_value.evidence: inferred: For in-cell LiP-MS, 90 μl of treated or untreated cells (approx. 3x1E6 cells) were mixed with 30 μl ice-cold PK solution (100 μM final PK concentration except in optimization experiments, PK dissolved in water). To determine the effect of PK on cells, 30 μl water were added instead.

technology_type.evidence: inferred: in-cell limited proteolysis-coupled mass spectrometry (in-cell LiP-MS).

technology_type.value: affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics
technology_type.evidence: inferred: Proteins were digested with Lys-C and trypsin at an enzyme substrate ratio of 1:100 shaking overnight at 37 °C.

inferred: DIA acquisition: Samples were injected into either (i) an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer equipped with a Waters nanoAQUITY UPLC System or (ii) an Orbitrap Eclipse Tribrid mass spectrometer equipped with a Waters nanoAQUITY UPLC System or (iii) Q Exactive Plus Hybrid Quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometer equipped with an EASY-nLC 1000 system or (iv) Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer equipped with a VanquishNeo System .
